# Wetlands in News (Oct 2026)

- **Natural oxbow lake of the Ganga**, fed by **3 channels**; a **freshwater** wetland (not saline; in Ballia, not Aligarh); on the **Central Asian Flyway**; supports groundwater recharge, fisheries and livelihoods.

- **CCPI 2027 – India 28th** (score **60.85**, rating **'Medium'**), **down 5** from **23rd (CCPI 2026)** and from **10th (CCPI 2025)** – a third straight fall; reasons: coal dependence, losses in **energy use** and **GHG emissions**.
- **CCPI 2026** (released at **COP30, Belém**, Nov 2025; by **Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network**; **63 countries + EU**): India **fell 13 places to 23rd** (score **61.31**; 'High' → **'Medium'** performer) – **no coal-exit timeline**, new coal block auctions; **ranks 1–3 vacant** (no country 'very high'), **Denmark 4th** (80.52), UK 5th, Morocco 6th; **Saudi Arabia last (67th)**.
- **Method:** CCPI published **since 2005**; weights **GHG emissions 40%**, **renewable energy 20%**, **energy use 20%**, **climate policy 20%**. CCPI ranks climate **performance**; Germanwatch's **Climate Risk Index** ranks climate **impact** (India 9th).
- **CCPI 2026 – positives cited for India:** 50% of installed capacity non-fossil (2025); **rooftop solar 20.8 GW (Sept 2025)**; **PAT mechanism (2012)**, BEE appliance labelling (2006).

- **SEEI 2024** (6th edition): by **BEE** (**Ministry of Power**) with **AEEE**, released **29 Aug 2025**, assessing **FY 2023-24**; **66 indicators**, **36 States/UTs**; States grouped by energy use; categories **Front Runners (>60%)**, Achievers, Contenders, Aspirants; agencies **EESL**, State Designated Agencies, DISCOMs.

- **Maharashtra** ranked **first** (top performer, Group 1, >15 MToE); **Andhra Pradesh** topped Group 2 (5-15 MToE), **Assam** Group 3 (1-5 MToE), **Tripura** Group 4 (<1 MToE); **Front Runners** included **AP, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu** (some digests wrongly call AP an "Achiever").

- India: **9th most affected** (8th in the earlier edition) – **430 events**, **$170 billion** losses, **80,000 deaths** (9.6% of global), about **1.3 billion** people affected; India **15th** for **2024 alone**.
- World (1995–2024): about **9,700** extreme-weather disasters, over **8,32,000** deaths and losses above **US$4.5 trillion**.
- **Germanwatch:** est. **1991**, **Bonn**; some items call this edition "CRI 2025".
- By **IQAir** (Switzerland), **8th edition**, released **24 March 2026**; **143 countries/territories**, **9,446 cities**.
- **Pakistan most polluted** country – **13x** WHO limit; then **Bangladesh, Tajikistan, Chad, DR Congo**; **India 6th** (from **5th** in 2024), PM2.5 **48.9 µg/m³**.
- **New Delhi** most polluted capital – **8th time** (Delhi is the Indian city most often in the news for poor air).
- Only **13** countries/territories and **14%** of cities met the **WHO PM2.5 guideline (5 µg/m³)**.

- **AP angle:** **Guntur** was joint 2nd in the 3-10 lakh category, 2026 (6th in 2025, when **Surat** was in the top 3 for the 2nd year).

- **NCAP:** launched **2019** by MoEFCC; **130 cities** in **24 States/UTs**; target first a **20–30% PM cut by 2024** (base **2017**), revised to **40% by 2026**; tracked on the **PRANA** portal; grants 2019-20 to 2025-26: **₹16,423.55 crore**; utilised **₹11,575.54 crore** (**70.5%**).

- Conferred by **President Droupadi Murmu** at **Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi**, on **11 Nov 2026**; survey by **MoHUA** (Minister **Manohar Lal**) under **SBM-Urban** – the world's largest urban cleanliness survey; **10th edition**, launched **20 December 2025**; field assessment **25 April – 31 May 2026**; about **4,700+ ULBs** assessed; theme "**Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel – Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath**".
- **Marks:** **12,500** – **10,500** on-ground assessment (with citizen feedback) + **2,000** certification (**ODF/ODF+/ODF++/Water+ 1,000**; **Garbage Free Cities 1,000**); **5 population categories** (below 20,000; 20,000–50,000; 50,000–3 lakh; 3–10 lakh; above 10 lakh) plus the **Super Swachh League**.
- **New this edition:** **Ganga Towns expanded to River Towns**; a separate matrix for **coastal areas**; **Swachh Shehar Jodis** (**72 mentor + 200 mentee** cities); round-the-year citizen feedback with more weight; focus on tourist, heritage and religious places.

- **AP's six award-winning ULBs:** **Greater Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Guntur, Tirupati, Rajamahendravaram** Municipal Corporations and **Kuppam** Municipality; Swachh Survekshan began in **2016 (73 cities)** under **SBM-Urban**; Swachh Survekshan **Grameen** is run by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
- By **MoHUA** (survey run by the **Quality Council of India**); **9th edition**; awards by **President Droupadi Murmu**; **4,589** cities ranked.

- **WWF + ZSL (Zoological Society of London)**, October 2026, titled **"The Science of Hope"**; **35,803** population trends, **5,790** vertebrate species.

- **The State of the World's Forests 2026** (FAO), "Restoring Forests and Landscapes - The Way Forward for a Sustainable Future": about **1.56 billion ha degraded**, nearly **10%** of world land, about **5.2 times** India's area; degraded forests **over 460 million ha**.
- **FAO:** est. **16 Oct 1945**, HQ **Rome**, DG **Qu Dongyu**; **World Food Day 16 October**; **COFO** = FAO's highest forestry body, meets **every two years**.
- **UNFCCC:** adopted **9 May 1992** (New York; opened at the Rio Earth Summit), in force **21 March 1994**; **198 Parties**; secretariat **Bonn, Germany**; **India ratified 1 November 1993**.

- **Arnab's landfall:** a **severe cyclonic storm** that formed in the **Bay of Bengal**; name proposed by **Bangladesh** ('Arnab' = **ocean/sea** in Bengali); forecast to cross near **Yanam**, it crossed on **28 Oct 2026** near **Narsapur** (about **20 km ENE of Narsapur**, **40 km SW of Yanam**), peak sustained winds up to **202 kmph**.

- **[02 Nov 2026] Cyclone Murasu:** a deep depression over the **Southwest Bay of Bengal** became Cyclonic Storm **Murasu on 1 Nov 2026**, forecast to cross between **Nellore and Narsapur** (AP); its rain damaged the **Polavaram Right Main Canal** lining (Eluru district). Name **India-proposed** – **Tamil** word for a **large war drum** used to announce wars, victories and royal orders (public alertness); previous cyclone **Arnab** (Bangladesh); next names **Akvan (Iran), Kani (Maldives), Elgaman (Oman), Seil (Oman), Sahab (Pakistan)**. Cyclones need **SST above 27°C** and a **Coriolis force**, so they **do not form near the equator**.

- **Naming:** **WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones** (**13 members**, **13 names each** = **169 names**; current list adopted **April 2020**); **RSMC New Delhi (IMD)** names North Indian Ocean cyclones; a name is assigned at **34 knots** (~**63 km/h**), **sequentially**, not by landfall country; a used name is not repeated.

- **India's first high-altitude Snow Leopard Safari:** launched **7 October 2026**, **Leh, Ladakh**, during **Wildlife Week**; **LG Vinai Kumar Saxena** flagged off **6 open-back vehicles**; Ladakh had approved India's first guided high-altitude wildlife safaris (Hemis NP, Changthang, Karakoram WLS; winter snow-leopard viewing; ~340 bird species; run by trained local youth).

- Implemented by **SHAN Society** (Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation; the SHAN Conservation Foundation was approved by the **Ladakh LG** under the Ladakh Dept of Environment and Forests) + **Ladakh Forest Department**.

- Launched by **PM Narendra Modi** on **9 April 2023** at **Mysuru** – **50 years of Project Tiger**; Union Cabinet approval **February 2024**; treaty-based organisation from **23 January 2025**; HQ/secretariat in **India (not Geneva)**.
# Protected-Area Numbers (2026)

- **India's first DNA-based** elephant count by the **Wildlife Institute of India** under **Project Elephant** (report **October 2025**, "Status of Elephants in India: DNA-based Synchronous All-India Population Estimation"): **22,446** (range 18,255–26,645) vs **27,312 (2017)** – ~**18% decline** (partly due to the new method); declines in the **Western Ghats** and **NE Hills & Brahmaputra Plains**; **Shivalik–Gangetic nearly unchanged**.
# Elephants
- **Dugong** (a keystone seagrass grazer): the **EAC** asked Tamil Nadu to revise the International Dugong Conservation Centre at **Manora, Thanjavur**.

- Notified by **MoEFCC**; in force **1 April 2026**, replacing **SWM Rules 2016** (which had **three** categories – wet, dry, domestic hazardous); under **Environment Protection Act, 1986**; also covers rural bodies; goal **zero landfill**, circular economy.
- Waste data: 620 lakh tonnes/year; ~1.85 lakh t/day generated; 1.14 lakh t/day processed; ~40,000 t/day landfilled.
- **Hierarchy**: **Prevention** → Reduction → Reuse → Recycling → Recovery → **Disposal (last resort)**.
- Centralised **portal** tracks the full lifecycle (reporting to **CPCB**); legacy dumpsites mapped by **31 October 2026**; **District Collectors** oversee landfills; special provisions for hilly areas and islands.

- **Four-way segregation** at source: **wet, dry, sanitary, special domestic hazardous (special-care)**.
| Bin colour | Waste stream |
|---|---|
| Green | Wet |
| Blue | Dry |
| Red | Sanitary (wrapped separately) |
| Black | Special-care |

- **Bulk generators**: more than **100 kg/day** waste, more than **40,000 litres/day** water use, or more than **20,000 sq m** built-up area – produce ~30% of solid waste; must **process on site** (**EBWGR** – on-site wet waste processing, portal registration, certification-based compliance).
- **Polluter Pays** – environmental compensation; higher landfill fees for unsegregated waste; CPCB frames guidelines, SPCBs enforce.

- Waste with calorific value **≥ 1,500 kcal/kg** → energy recovery; industries raise **RDF** use **5% → 15%** over six years; **biomining/bioremediation** for legacy dumps; **tourist user charges** in hill/island areas.

- **Conceived by NITI Aayog**; launched **2021**; **International Container Transshipment Terminal at Galathea Bay**, greenfield (dual-use) international airport, township, gas and solar plant; development area 166 sq km; near the **Six Degree Channel** and **Malacca Strait**; aim: cut dependence on **Colombo, Singapore, Port Klang**; cost first put at **₹72,000 crore**.

- Concerns: ~**130 sq km rainforest** (lakhs of trees felled); ~**700 ha** allegedly in **ICRZ 2019** prohibited zones; **Giant Leatherback Turtle** nesting at Galathea Bay; coral reefs; high seismic/tsunami zone (2004). Tribes **Shompen (PVTG) and Nicobarese**; Shompen Policy 2015; NCST under Article 338A(9). The NGT demanded strict compliance with the clearance.
- **National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme (2025):** **₹150 crore**; **Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand**; **CWC** does GLOF risk indexing.
- Whole Himalaya: **2,843** glacial lakes and water bodies monitored by satellite – **1,435** grew, 1,008 shrank.
- **IMD cloudburst**: at least **100 mm in one hour** (not 50 mm) over **20-30 sq km**.

- **MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes):** launched **5 June 2023** by **MoEFCC**, after India joined the **Mangrove Alliance for Climate (COP27, 2022)**; objective: **increase mangrove cover and conserve mangrove ecosystems** along the coastline and on salt-pan lands, with livelihoods for local communities; target about **54,000 ha by 2028** (restore **540 sq km**; ~**4.5 million tonnes** carbon-sequestration potential); **₹100 crore**; **Andhra Pradesh ranked 2nd** in mangrove restoration (July 2026).

- **Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999**; Rules **2002**; in force **15 September 2003**; registrations from **2004-05** (first: Darjeeling Tea); Rules amended **2025**.
- **GI Registry: Chennai** (under the **CGPDTM**), all-India jurisdiction; administered by **DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce and Industry)**.
- **Karbi Anglong ginger (GI, Assam)** – 1.2 MT trial export to London; **Joha rice** – UK and Italy.
- India sets its target in **emissions intensity** (per unit of GDP), **not absolute emissions**; **net zero by 2070** was announced at **COP26, Glasgow (2021)**.
# China's Targets
- **30 June 2026**: installed capacity **5,48,858 MW (548.86 GW)**; non-fossil **54.18%** (52.57% in Feb 2026) – already beyond the **NDC target of 50% by 2030** (reached June 2025).
- The **first CITES CoP in Central Asia**; **77 species** added to the CITES Appendices (incl. sharks and iguanas); proposals to weaken protection rejected – **rhino horn and ivory trade bans stay**.

- **Two tripartite MoUs** on **24 Sep 2026** at the **9th India International Water Week** (**22–26 Sep 2026**, **Bharat Mandapam**, New Delhi; theme "Climate Resilient Water Management"; Ministry of Jal Shakti): **CWC**, **Gujarat's Kalpasar Department**, **Deltares (Netherlands)**, **Delft University of Technology**; **CWC:** est. **1945**, HQ **New Delhi**, **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.

- **GIB:** *Ardeotis nigriceps*; **IUCN Critically Endangered**; **WPA Schedule I**; **CITES Appendix I**; also **CMS**; **Rajasthan State Bird**; arid/semi-arid grasslands; global population below 200; lays **one egg** at a time; main threat **power-line collisions**.
- **Captive breeding:** **Ramdevra and Sam (Jaisalmer)**; Species Recovery Programme under **IDWH** (100% central assistance), with WII.

- **29 December 2025**: the 20 November definition order **stayed**; an expert committee to be formed (bench CJI **Surya Kant**, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M. Pancholi) – the SC expert committee, chaired by **Kanchan Devi**, is to define the range's limits (report by **31 Aug 2026**); refused Haryana jungle safari DPR until Aravalli is defined.

- **QS 2023**: **Pakistan** the only other SAARC nation in the top 500 – **three** universities.
- **NITI Aayog**: **1 January 2015** (replaced the Planning Commission); Chair **PM**; Vice-Chair **Ashok Kumar Lahiri**; CEO **Anurag Jain**.

- **Thwaites Glacier** (**West Antarctica**, the **'Doomsday Glacier'**): full collapse → ~**65 cm** sea-level rise; fracture length **165 km (2002) → 335 km (2022)**; two-stage fracture; Eastern Ice Shelf pinned to a seabed ridge.
